html:
The Gurindji are an Aboriginal people of the Victoria River district of the Northern Territory, in grassland country about 460 kilometres southwest of Katherine. They are best known for the Wave Hill walk-off, a turning point in the fight for Aboriginal land rights.

In the 1880s their land was taken for Wave Hill Station, a huge cattle run later owned by the British Vestey company. Gurindji people worked the cattle for rations and little or no pay, and lived in poor camps.

  • 1966: led by Vincent Lingiari, about 200 Gurindji workers and their families walked off the station. A strike over wages became a demand for their land.
  • 1967: they set up camp at Wattie Creek (Daguragu), on their own country.
  • 1975: Prime Minister Gough Whitlam poured a handful of soil into Lingiari's hand to mark the return of part of their land.

The walk-off helped bring about the Aboriginal Land Rights Act of 1976 for the Northern Territory. Neighbours include the Mudburra, Bilinara and Ngarinman. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
